schema_note: Digital Product Factory Pro Competitive Upgrade Roadmap, established 2026-09-12. This is the durable strategic source of truth so a future Claude session cannot lose the strategic direction: quality/reliability/design/publishing/simplicity, NOT more product breadth, until these six upgrades are complete. Status values: NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, VERIFYING, COMPLETE_LOCKED. Do not reorder upgrades without a real dependency reason (see each entry's `dependencies`). Do not begin an upgrade after the current one unless the owner explicitly approves skipping ahead.
vision: A beginner should go from IDEA -> MARKET OPPORTUNITY -> PRODUCT -> PROFESSIONAL DESIGN -> COVER -> VISUALS -> QA -> PREVIEW -> APPROVAL -> MULTIPLE EXPORT FORMATS -> READY-TO-SELL PACKAGE with as little technical knowledge and manual work as possible. The customer experience stays: Create -> Preview -> Approve -> Download. Digital Product Factory Pro is not a Designrr clone -- it is a complete AI-assisted digital-product production system competing on: Factory Market Advantage before creation, multiple product types, one-click production, free/local resources first with controlled paid-AI fallback, automatic QA, professional covers and interiors, protected working generators, automatic packaging, ready-to-sell outputs, and minimal technical interaction.
standing_priority: QUALITY -> RELIABILITY -> DESIGN -> PUBLISHING -> SIMPLICITY, not additional product types, until all six upgrades are COMPLETE_LOCKED. Do not add a new product generator unless the owner explicitly approves one.

upgrade_1_cover_system.name: Global Professional Cover System
upgrade_1_cover_system.objective: Every Factory product with an image-based cover follows one policy: PEXELS FIRST -> relevance/quality gate -> paid AI fallback -> professional template/procedural fallback where appropriate -> final cover QA -> approve -> Function Lock.
upgrade_1_cover_system.why_it_matters_competitively: The cover is the single most important sales asset for a self-published digital product -- a weak or irrelevant cover undercuts every other quality investment the Factory makes. Free-first sourcing with a real quality gate keeps costs low without shipping poor covers, which is exactly the discipline Designrr does not enforce for the customer automatically.
upgrade_1_cover_system.current_foundation: services/cover_source_policy.py (PEXELS FIRST gate + paid AI fallback), services/cover_agent.py + services/product_cover_agent.py + services/cover_quality_agent.py (shared HTML cover engine + final rendered-cover QA) for Ebook (Cover Editor route)/Word Search/Crossword; services/coloring_book/final_cover_qa.py (new, 2026-09-12 -- Coloring Book's own automatic-build final QA adapter); services/ebook_photo_cover.py + services/ebook_customer_path.py (Ebook's separate, real, raster-measurement-based guided-flow QA -- verified equivalent to final cover QA, not routed through the shared agent); services/planner/design_rating.py::rate_planner_design + services/editor_in_chief_planner.py::review_planner (Faith/Budget Planner's real, pixel-measurement-based final QA gating export_ready at /export-product -- verified equivalent, not routed through the shared agent).
upgrade_1_cover_system.gap_remaining: Ebook's PRIMARY guided-flow cover system (services/ebook_photo_cover.py) still has no AI fallback at all -- Pexels or customer upload only; bridging it to AI would mean integrating two structurally different rendering engines (PIL-raster vs HTML/CSS), a larger project deliberately not attempted yet. Coloring Book and Crossword's automatic/initial builds still do not call the paid AI cover step by design (pre-existing cost-avoidance, not a gap). The extended Pexels-first policy for Word Search/Crossword/Ebook and the Coloring Book final-QA adapter are implemented and passing all tests but NOT YET committed/pushed -- awaiting owner review.
upgrade_1_cover_system.function_lock_impact: word_search, crossword, and coloring_book are LOCKED functions; all three were explicitly UNLOCKED for this work (services/cover_agent.py, services/product_cover_agent.py, services/cover_quality_agent.py, services/cover_source_policy.py added as real shared_code_dependencies -- a previously-undeclared gap found and corrected). ebook, faith_planner, and budget_planner are PROTECTED (not LOCKED); their existing protected suites were re-verified green. None may be RELOCKED until the owner approves committing the code that becomes their new last-known-good commit (Rule 9: never manufacture a last-known-good hash).
acceptance_criteria: Every image-cover product either uses the shared Pexels-first policy or has a verified-equivalent product-specific final QA authority (documented in PROTECTED_GENERATOR_RULE.md's QA contract map).
A weak/irrelevant Pexels candidate is never accepted merely because Pexels returned one.
cover_source and paid_ai_used are recorded honestly for every generated cover, reflecting what the customer actually received.
Final rendered-cover QA runs for every product before a cover is considered finished; a broken/incomplete cover fails clearly rather than shipping silently.
No product's existing customer behavior changed except the cover source/quality gate itself.
upgrade_1_cover_system.customer_path_proof_required: Real (mocked-provider) generation of an Ebook, Word Search, Crossword, and Coloring Book cover each passing final QA; a Faith/Budget Planner export reaching export_ready; zero real paid AI calls during verification.
upgrade_1_cover_system.status_detail: COMPLETE as of 2026-09-13, commit 1de91dc, pushed to origin/main. Full Release Gate PASS -- 2804 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, 0 paid API calls -- confirmed on two separate fresh, uninterrupted runs (2026-09-12 and 2026-09-13). Fast Stability Gate PASS -- 160 passed, 666 subtests. Word Search, Crossword, and Coloring Book relocked at ab6b923 (the real final implementation commit). Ebook, Faith Planner, and Budget Planner's own existing final-QA systems confirmed genuinely equivalent to the shared agent, documented in PROTECTED_GENERATOR_RULE.md's QA contract map -- not forced through a redesign. Live site confirmed reachable post-deploy; deeper live verification (deployed version number, a real customer cover generation) was not attempted -- no invite code available or requested. Known, deliberately out-of-scope gaps for a future decision: Ebook's PRIMARY guided-flow cover system still has no AI fallback (Pexels/upload only); Coloring Book and Crossword's automatic/initial builds still do not auto-call paid AI by design (pre-existing cost-avoidance, unchanged).
upgrade_1_cover_system.next_step: Upgrade 2 (Designrr-Quality Interior Themes and Templates) requires the owner's explicit approval before starting.

upgrade_2_interior_themes.name: Designrr-Quality Interior Themes and Templates
upgrade_2_interior_themes.objective: A professional, reusable interior theme/template system controlling typography, headings/subheadings, colors, chapter openers, section breaks, callout boxes, quote blocks, checklists, tables, margins, spacing, image placement, TOC styling, and page furniture -- so a customer gets a professionally designed product by picking a theme, not by manually designing every page.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.why_it_matters_competitively: Designrr's core strength is templated interior design. Matching or exceeding that with automated, theme-driven layout (rather than one-size-fits-all output) is required for the Factory to be perceived as equally or more professional, without asking beginners to make design decisions.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.current_foundation: services/planner/themes.py + services/planner/cover.py already implement a working theme-driven design system for Planners (palette, typography, cover art recipe per theme) -- the closest existing precedent. Ebook has ebook_design_workspace.py/ebook_visual_pipeline.py for layout, but no equivalent named theme-family system across Business/Wellness/Faith/Education/etc.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.gap_remaining: No cross-product theme-family system exists yet for Ebook/Word Search/Crossword/Coloring Book interiors matching the planner precedent's depth (only Planners have real theme families today). Target theme families (Business/Professional, Wellness, Faith, Education, Children's, Personal Development, Finance, Minimal/Modern, Luxury/Premium, Feminine, Masculine, Vintage, Bold/Contemporary) do not exist for Ebook interiors.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.function_lock_impact: Not yet started -- to be determined during Phase A (read-only audit) of this upgrade. Ebook is PROTECTED; whichever shared files a theme system introduces must be declared as dependencies for every affected function before implementation, per standing Function Lock discipline.
acceptance_criteria: A customer can choose a theme and receive a professionally designed product without manual per-page design.
Themes improve readability and professional presentation, not merely decoration.
At least a first set of theme families ships with real typography/color/layout differentiation, verified visually.
Existing customer-facing behavior for products not touched by a given theme change is unaffected.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.customer_path_proof_required: Real generation of the same content under at least two different themes, showing genuinely different, professional typography/layout -- not just a color swap.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.status_detail: Not started. Upgrade 1 must finish first per roadmap order.
upgrade_2_interior_themes.next_step: Do not begin until the owner approves starting Upgrade 2. When approved, start with a read-only Phase A audit of existing theme-like systems (services/planner/themes.py, ebook_design_workspace.py) before any implementation.

upgrade_3_visual_editing.name: Easy Visual Editing
upgrade_3_visual_editing.objective: Lightweight, beginner-friendly editing for cover, images, fonts, colors, theme, title/subtitle, author, safe layout choices, and spacing -- an Edit -> Preview -> Approve loop, not desktop-publishing software.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.why_it_matters_competitively: Automation-first is the Factory's advantage, but customers still need a simple way to make it their own. Over-exposing technical controls would make the Factory feel harder than Designrr, which is explicitly the opposite of the goal.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.current_foundation: The Cover Editor (/cover/*) already provides limited editing (style, palette, font, image regeneration, text position) for Ebook/Word Search/Crossword/Coloring Book, gated by the existing artifact DRAFT/APPROVED/LOCKED lifecycle (services/quality/artifact_state.py) so an edit cannot silently bypass export QA.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.gap_remaining: No unified, beginner-simple editing surface exists across products yet; today's Cover Editor is the only real editing capability, and it predates the theme system Upgrade 2 will introduce.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.function_lock_impact: saved_projects (PROTECTED) and services/quality/artifact_state.py's mutation rules are central to this upgrade -- any editor must route through the existing DRAFT/APPROVED/LOCKED contract, never bypass it.
acceptance_criteria: A customer can change cover, images, fonts, colors, theme, title/subtitle, author, and safe layout/spacing choices without technical knowledge.
No edit can silently produce a product that fails export QA -- the same final QA authority from Upgrade 1/2 always re-runs.
The editing UI stays to a small, guided set of controls -- not a general-purpose design tool.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.customer_path_proof_required: A real edit-preview-approve cycle that changes a real product's cover/theme/typography and still passes final QA and export.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.status_detail: Not started. Depends on Upgrades 1 and 2.
upgrade_3_visual_editing.next_step: Do not begin until Upgrades 1 and 2 are COMPLETE_LOCKED and the owner approves starting Upgrade 3.

upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.name: Professional Multi-Format Publishing
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.objective: Expand validated output beyond PDF/ZIP to Professional PDF, EPUB, Kindle-compatible output, KDP-ready output where appropriate, and print-ready output where appropriate -- each with its own validation contract, reusing approved content/layout rather than building a second design system.
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.why_it_matters_competitively: Multi-format, marketplace-ready export (KDP, EPUB/Kindle) is a concrete, checkable competitive differentiator beyond what a single-format export tool offers.
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.current_foundation: services/kdp/preflight.py and existing KDP-related tests (test_kdp_foundations_pass1.py, test_kdp_preflight_pass2.py) already establish some KDP-readiness checking for existing PDF export. No EPUB or Kindle-format pipeline exists yet.
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.gap_remaining: EPUB/Kindle export and their validation contracts do not exist. Print-ready bleed/margin/resolution validation beyond current KDP preflight is unconfirmed in scope.
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.function_lock_impact: pdf_zip_export (PROTECTED) is the highest-blast-radius shared packaging path per the Shared-Service Dependency Map -- any new export format must be additive, not a rewrite of services/packaging.py.
acceptance_criteria: Each new format has its own real validation contract (e.g. EPUB must validate as EPUB; KDP/print output respects dimensions, bleed, margins, cover requirements, pagination, fonts, image resolution).
No format is produced by a blind file conversion without validation.
Existing PDF/ZIP behavior is unchanged.
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.customer_path_proof_required: A real product exported in at least one new format, validated against that format's own contract, not just 'the file exists.'
upgrade_4_multi_format_publishing.next_step: Do not begin until Upgrades 1-3 are COMPLETE_LOCKED (or the owner explicitly approves reordering) and Upgrade 4 is explicitly approved to start.

upgrade_5_flipbook.name: Flipbook
upgrade_5_flipbook.objective: A polished, digital page-turning presentation built from an already-approved Factory product, as an additional output option -- never regenerating or altering the approved PDF, which remains the source of truth.
upgrade_5_flipbook.why_it_matters_competitively: A page-turning digital preview is a common, expected format for buyers evaluating a digital product before or alongside PDF delivery.
upgrade_5_flipbook.current_foundation: No Flipbook capability exists yet in this codebase.
upgrade_5_flipbook.function_lock_impact: Must not alter or destabilize the approved PDF/product pipeline -- the Flipbook reads from an already-approved artifact, it does not produce one, so it should not need to touch any currently LOCKED generator's own code.
acceptance_criteria: Flipbook output is generated from the already-approved PDF/product, not a re-generation.
The approved PDF is provably unchanged (byte-identical or otherwise verified) after Flipbook creation.
Flipbook is offered as an additional option, never a replacement for the standard export.
upgrade_5_flipbook.customer_path_proof_required: A real approved product converted to Flipbook form with the original PDF verified unchanged.
upgrade_5_flipbook.next_step: Do not begin until Upgrade 4 is COMPLETE_LOCKED (or the owner explicitly approves reordering) and Upgrade 5 is explicitly approved to start.

upgrade_6_one_click_experience.name: One-Click Customer Experience
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.objective: Orchestrate Research -> Opportunity -> Title -> Outline -> Content -> Visuals -> Cover -> Interior Design -> QA -> Preview -> Preflight -> Export -> Package behind a minimal customer path: choose what to build, answer a few simple questions, click Create Product, review, approve, download -- with customer-friendly failure messages and safe automatic correction, never exposing technical internals.
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.why_it_matters_competitively: This is the ultimate expression of 'easier than Designrr' -- the governing design philosophy for every other upgrade, not just a final feature.
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.current_foundation: Factory Market Advantage already helps customers decide what to build before creation. Individual product generators, cover policy (Upgrade 1), and QA agents already exist as the pieces to orchestrate.
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.gap_remaining: No single orchestrated one-click flow exists yet spanning research through packaging with unified customer-friendly error handling across all product types.
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.function_lock_impact: Touches essentially every product function as an orchestration layer -- every affected LOCKED function must go through UNLOCK -> CHANGE -> PROTECTED TESTS -> REQUIRED GATES -> CUSTOMER-PATH PROOF -> RELOCK individually; this upgrade must not become an excuse to bulk-unlock everything at once.
acceptance_criteria: A customer can go from idea to downloaded, ready-to-sell product via: choose what to build, answer a few simple questions, click Create Product, review, approve, download.
No provider error messages, stack traces, API variable names, internal file names, Python errors, or technical QA codes are ever shown to the customer.
Automatic correction is attempted where safe; if a passing product cannot be produced, the Factory stops clearly rather than shipping a bad product.
This upgrade governs, and does not contradict, the design philosophy already applied in Upgrades 1-5.
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.customer_path_proof_required: A real, real end-to-end one-click generation for at least one product type, with a customer-friendly failure-mode demonstration (a deliberately induced failure shows a clean message, not an internal error).
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.status_detail: Not started. This is also the governing design philosophy for Upgrades 1-5, not only a final feature.
upgrade_6_one_click_experience.next_step: Do not begin until Upgrades 1-5 are COMPLETE_LOCKED (or the owner explicitly approves reordering) and Upgrade 6 is explicitly approved to start.

marketing_factory_track.note: Virtual Marketing Factory Pro is a THIRD roadmap axis, separate from upgrades 1-6 (product/design quality) and Upgrade 0 (execution infrastructure). It is DESIGN ONLY. The authoritative architecture is UPGRADE_0_PRODUCTION_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT.md sections 27-35.
marketing_factory_track.north_star_pipeline: FIND IT -> BUILD IT -> APPROVE IT -> STORE IT -> MARKET IT -> SELL IT -> IMPROVE IT

stage_owners.store_it: assets table + shared object storage (Upgrade 0 Phase 0B-3)
stage_owners.sell_distribute_it: Listing Factory + Pin Factory Pro + future Email/Social/Website

marketing_factory_track.hard_precondition: Marketing may NEVER begin before a product is COMPLETE/APPROVED: product QA, Editor-in-Chief, preflight, export, valid deliverable, approved asset records, stable storage keys and confirmed customer download availability. A marketing failure must never affect product completion, approval, PDF/ZIP availability, Saved Projects, customer downloads or artifact integrity.
marketing_factory_track.infrastructure_prerequisite: Implement ONLY after the storage/Postgres/worker migration is production-stable: 0B-3 storage -> 0B-4 Postgres -> 0B-5 job manager + worker -> 0C ebook worker migration -> 0D three successful live ebook builds -> 0E remaining workflows.

versions.v1: Marketing Profile; Virtual Marketing Manager recommendation; Marketplace Listing Generator; Marketing Kit Generator; Pin Factory Pro integration; Marketing Inspector / Preflight
versions.v2: Email campaign builder; Social campaign builder; Campaign calendar; Marketing Command Center; reusable promotional templates; bundle recommendations
versions.v3: Marketing analytics; performance comparison; automatic recommendations; A/B variations; Marketing Autopilot; cross-product intelligence; automatic campaign refreshes

marketing_factory_track.pin_factory_pro: An INTERNAL distribution engine under the Virtual Marketing Manager, not a separate top-level product. Consumes approved asset records, never filesystem paths. A Pinterest failure must not revert product status, remove approved assets, break downloads, alter PDF/ZIP, alter product QA state or alter Saved Projects.

v1.8.0.what_it_fixes: A live Resume Build for 'Container Gardening for Beginners' exceeded the Render web service memory limit because the book was written inside the process that serves pages.
v1.8.0.architecture_decision: Render Workflows, not an always-on Background Worker. Product generation is bursty: a Workflows task starts on demand with up to 1 CPU and 4 GB and is billed only while running ($0.20/CPU-hour + $0.05/GB-hour, verified 2026-09-17), where an always-on worker with 4 GB is $85 a month whether or not anyone is building a book.
v1.8.0.switch: FACTORY_EXECUTION_MODE=workflow on the web service. Unset means the v1.7.29 behaviour, which is also what every local Windows checkout uses.
v1.8.0.rollback: Delete FACTORY_EXECUTION_MODE on the web service. No data migration either way; both modes use the same job rows, PostgreSQL and R2.
